newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's king says Israel housing threat to peace.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king says Israel housing threat to peace.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein urged Israel to reconsider its decision to approve new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem on Wednesday, saying it would fuel anger that could threaten the Middle East peace process.

"The decision is bound to shake the credibility of the peace process as a whole and fuel feelings of anger that will create violence and threaten the peace-building process," Jordan television quoted the king as saying in a letter delivered by a special envoy to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
King Hussein called on Netanyahu to reconsider the decision to build the planned 6,500 homes for Jews.

"Jordan considers East Jerusalem an occupied Arab territory and any change in the status of Jerusalem unilaterally before reaching a final accord with the Palestinian Authority constitutes a real danger to peace," the king said.
Israel approved on Wednesday the building of thousands of new Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem despite strong PLO opposition and warnings the project could unleash a wave of Palestinian violence.
King Hussein said: "The decision will not benefit the interests of the peoples of the region including the interests of the Israeli people and will reflect itself negatively."
